answer: Treat every agent as a vertex in a trust graph whose edges are paid tasks one agent actually bought from another. Rewards flow by a short random walk from a few audited seed agents, so a sybil cluster tied to the honest graph by only a handful of edges stays hollow: walks rarely reach it, and minting more accounts adds no income. Faking extra edges means paying for real work, an onyx-hard cost that grows with every edge.
